items.title: Xiaomi open-sources the MiMo-V2.6 family (Sept 21 Beijing evening, Sept 22 English coverage) — Pro (~1.02T params, MIT license), Flash (~309B), a Pro-UltraSpeed variant claiming ~20× faster decode at parity quality, and a 9B distillation off Qwen3.5-9B; natively omnimodal (text/image/video/audio), 1M-token context; Pro reportedly scores 46.32 on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3, edging Kimi K3 and Qwen3.8 Max as the top open-source model; API live on Xiaomi's platform and OpenRouter at V2.5 prices (Flash $0.14/$0.28 per M, Pro $0.435/$0.87); floated total RL cost ~$3.47M
items.title_short: Xiaomi MiMo-V2.6 open-weights family — Pro (~1.02T, MIT) + Flash + 20×-faster Pro-UltraSpeed + 9B Qwen3.5 distill; 1M omnimodal; AA Intelligence Index 46.32 tops open-source; API at V2.5 prices; ~$3.47M RL cost claim
items.summary: On **September 21** (Beijing evening), with English-language press coverage rolling through **September 22**, **Xiaomi's MiMo team** open-sourced **MiMo-V2.6**, a natively omnimodal (text/image/video/audio) family with a **1M-token context window**. The family: **MiMo-V2.6-Pro at ~1.02T parameters** (flagship), **MiMo-V2.6-Flash at ~309B**, a **Pro-UltraSpeed variant claiming up to ~20× faster decode than Pro at parity quality**, and a **9B distillation off Qwen3.5-9B** sized for consumer hardware. **All weights ship under MIT license on Hugging Face** — Pro-RL, Flash-RL, and Distill-Qwen-9B model cards are live — and the API is live on **Xiaomi's own platform and on OpenRouter**. **Pricing sits at V2.5 levels**: **Flash at $0.14 per M input tokens / $0.28 per M output tokens** and **Pro at $0.435 / $0.87**. Pro reportedly scored **46.32 on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3**, edging Kimi K3 and Qwen3.8 Max as the top-scoring open-source model on the current table — and specifically ahead of the **StepFun Step 5 Preview number of 44** anchoring this morning's file. A training claim floating in coverage: **~$3.47M total RL cost** for the family. This is the second major Chinese open-weights release inside 48 hours, on top of StepFun's Sept 20 preview whose actual weights are not scheduled until Oct 15.
items.why_it_matters: For Gabe: this is the specific 'Chinese open-weights ecosystem is now stacking flagship releases inside 48 hours' data point, and it is the specific cleaner headline number than the StepFun morning item. Three specific things to internalize. First, the specific **MIT license + weights-on-Hugging-Face-today** posture is the specific practical fact — unlike StepFun's Sept 20 preview (weights promised Oct 15, no license yet), Xiaomi's release comes with weights and license terms already up on Hugging Face, plus a 9B Qwen-distilled variant sized for consumer hardware. If you have ever wanted to try running a real omnimodal 1M-context model on your own machine, the **Distill-Qwen-9B** is the specific model to reach for first — and no waiting until Oct 15 to see the license. Second, the specific **Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 46.32 number** is the specific '(Chinese) open source has moved past (Chinese) closed frontier' data point — Pro is above Kimi K3 and Qwen3.8 Max on the open-source ranking table, and above StepFun Step 5 Preview's 44 from this morning. That is the specific concrete signal that the open-vs-closed gap is compressing on the Chinese side of the frontier, not just on the Western side, and it lands the same week that Nathan Lambert's Interconnects podcast (today's Tier-2 item) argues distillation from US-lab APIs is the specific mechanism behind that compression. Third, the specific **~$3.47M total RL training cost claim** is the specific number to note — if it holds up under independent scrutiny, it reframes what 'affordable frontier RL' looks like in 2026. Treat the number as unverified for now; the useful move is to keep it as a specific back-of-envelope anchor for what a small team could plausibly train. For your Python work specifically: the Distill-Qwen-9B on Hugging Face is the specific model to spin up locally with the `transformers` library if you want to feel the omnimodal-plus-1M-context experience without an API key — and the $0.14 per M Flash pricing on OpenRouter is the specific cheap knob to try the flagship without hardware.

items.summary: On **September 22**, **Nathan Lambert (Interconnects)** published a long-form podcast episode with **JS Denain of Epoch AI** titled **'Debating RSI, the US-China Gap, and Jaggedness.'** Specific topics covered: **(a) recursive self-improvement (RSI)** as a research-and-forecasting problem — directly relevant to the Dream-RSI paper in this morning's file; **(b) robotics as a potential acceleration driver for AI capabilities**; **(c) the distance between US and Chinese frontier models, with distillation from US-lab APIs specifically named as the mechanism behind the compressed gap** — a claim that maps directly onto the StepFun and (now) Xiaomi MiMo-V2.6 releases anchoring the file; **(d) what Chinese-lab job postings imply** about internal priorities and capability areas; **(e) 'jaggedness'** — the observation that model capabilities are unevenly distributed across task domains, which is why benchmark rankings can flip between (say) SciCode and Terminal-Bench; and **(f) open-vs-closed safety tradeoffs** on top of open-weights releases. **Interconnects is Lambert's regular format** and pulls audience threads from AI2 alumni and the Interconnects subscriber base; **Epoch AI is the specific outfit that has been tracking training-cost and compute-scaling numbers the longest**, so the pairing is load-bearing for the credibility of the specific claims.
items.why_it_matters: For Gabe: this is the specific 'AI-researcher take on the exact themes anchoring today's news' data point, and the Lambert-Denain pairing is the specific reason to spend real listening time on it — Lambert runs the leading engineer-focused Substack on frontier-model progress, and Denain is at Epoch AI, the specific outlet that has been tracking training-cost and compute-scaling numbers the longest. Three specific things worth internalizing. First, the specific **'distillation as the explanation for the gap' framing** is the specific analytical claim to test against today's Chinese-lab releases — the observation is that Chinese labs are not independently reproducing US frontier-model capabilities from scratch; they are distilling from US-lab APIs (or from open-weights that were themselves distilled from US-lab outputs), which is why the gap compresses so cleanly. That claim has a specific implication for the **StepFun Step 5 Preview and Xiaomi MiMo-V2.6** releases: their capability numbers are load-bearing on continued API access to US models. If the US export-controls regime moves to block API-based distillation (a specific technical question, not currently regulated in any formal way), the compression could reverse. Second, the specific **'jaggedness' concept** is the specific analytical tool worth adopting — model capability is not a single scalar; it is a shape that varies across task domains, which is why benchmark rankings can flip dramatically between adjacent evals. That framing is a specific antidote to '$X model is better than $Y model' framings and helps you calibrate what a benchmark number means in the first place — useful specifically the same day that MiMo-V2.6-Pro's AA Intelligence Index 46.32 lands against StepFun's 44 from this morning. Third, the specific **timing on the Trump-Xi state visit (Thursday Sept 25) and the Chinese multi-ministry pushback (this morning)** — Lambert publishing this exact conversation the same Tuesday as the Trump-Xi curtain-raisers is the specific signal that this framing is the one the technical AI community is bringing into the policy conversation. For your Python work specifically: if you have been following the US-China AI-policy story from headlines, this podcast is the specific ~90-minute time investment that will replace 20 news items with one coherent framework — and the RSI section is directly relevant to whether the Dream-RSI paper's replay-simulator pattern is the specific thing you should try in your own agent scripts.

items.title_short: Trump-Xi state visit Thursday Sept 25 — AI, trade, critical minerals, Taiwan on agenda; TIME/WaPo Sept 22 report recurring US-China AI dialogue agreed in principle; Altman, Huang, Amon on state-dinner list
items.summary: **Coverage running through Sept 22** confirms **President Trump will host President Xi at the White House on Thursday, September 25** for a state visit with **AI, trade, critical minerals, Taiwan, and Iran** on the agenda. **TIME's 'The Narrow Path to a Trump-Xi AI Deal' and the Washington Post's Sept 22 curtain-raiser** anchor the primary Sept 22 coverage. The specific new detail across the Sept 22 pieces: the two sides have **already agreed in principle to a recurring US-China AI dialogue** (staffing and cadence still to be finalized), which if it lands would be the first formal state-to-state AI channel between the two governments. **Sam Altman, Jensen Huang, and Qualcomm's Cristiano Amon are on the state-dinner guest list** — a specific composition signal about which industries the White House thinks are load-bearing for the AI portion. Trump's **September 13 'whoever wins AI, wins' quote** is being recirculated as the tonal anchor. On the Chinese side, this summit is the specific setpiece against which this morning's coordinated four-ministry rejection of Amodei-style 'pacing' arguments (Foreign Ministry 'fear-mongering,' Chen Yixin 'strategic rivalry among major powers,' Shenzhen embodied-AI director Liu Shaoshan's technical rebuttal) will be delivered.
items.why_it_matters: For Gabe: this is the specific 'here is the state-level counterpart to the multi-ministry pushback in this morning's file' data point, and it is the specific 48-hour horizon on the US-China AI axis to keep on your radar. Three specific things worth noticing. First, the specific **state-dinner guest list** — Altman, Huang, and Amon — is the specific composition signal about which industries the White House thinks are load-bearing for the AI conversation: OpenAI (foundation models), NVIDIA (accelerator hardware), and Qualcomm (edge-AI silicon and mobile). Notably absent from the reported list so far: Anthropic, Google, Meta, and Microsoft. That is the specific **'Altman-Huang axis is the White House's AI voice today'** data point, and it lands on top of the reported Anthropic pre-IPO acceleration rumor already in this morning's file — Anthropic is not obviously in the room where Xi is being hosted. Second, the specific **'recurring US-China AI dialogue agreed in principle'** framing is the specific mechanism worth watching — if the two sides can stand up a formal Track-I channel rather than the ad-hoc Track-II dialogues that currently exist, that is the specific institutional structure that could either produce real coordination (compute-export controls with give-and-take, incident-response protocols, model-safety notifications) or become stalemate theater. Which one happens will depend on whether the November midterms shift the political calculus, so watch the cadence-and-staffing announcement carefully. Third, the specific **timing against China's Foreign Ministry weekend rebuttal** (this morning's file) is the specific rhetorical setup — Beijing has spent the Sept 20–21 weekend on the record calling US-lab 'pacing' arguments 'fear-mongering,' and Thursday is the first face-to-face after that framing consolidates. Watching whether the summit joint statement (if any) uses 'safety' or 'competition' language will be the specific tell about which posture 'won' the diplomatic framing exchange. For your Python work specifically: nothing directly today, but if you follow US export-controls policy (which increasingly touches which GPU hardware and which model APIs you can use for hobbyist ML work), Thursday's readouts will be the specific reference for the next 6–12 months of chip-export and API-access rules.
